input: on the human imitation project how's that going I want have browser use and webcam also be a subject as well as the writing. and it's not just prompt as the parameter to change, it can also be code. I think there can be shared feedback between the human detector and the human imitator agents.

errors.what: Imitator fitness was AUROC, which saturates at 1.0 and ranked no candidate; switched to the detector's mean log-odds. The ceiling search repeated the same mistake and was rerun with cross-validated log-loss.
Endpoint bug in generate(): de-duplicating timestamps kept the last clock tick and dropped the true endpoint; caught by a test, main run restarted.
Process pool oversubscribed 4 CPUs through OpenMP threads in boosted trees; set one thread per worker.
pkill -f with a pattern matching the invoking shell's own command line killed the shell (exit 144) twice.

doc_friction.issue: CI on a research-only PR went red from main (xero-invoice-csv-check FAQ JSON-LD drift after #8669/#8671); nothing points to a way to see that main itself is red before debugging the PR.
The 120s foreground limit note is accurate; a long experiment also needs OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 when it uses a process pool with scikit-learn boosted trees, which is not mentioned.

deviations.why: The brief came from the owner directly (status plus new direction), so the run skipped the router's draw and took the research track; the direction was written into track 11 as milestones 9 to 11 and the first one was built in the same PR rather than a direction-only edit.
Ported the FAQ fix from open PR #8694 (another session's) into this research PR to get CI green, as the drive-to-green rules say, instead of waiting for #8694 to merge.

notes: Reported track 11 status; recorded the owner's 2026-10-20 direction (browser use and webcam subjects, code as a free parameter, shared detector-imitator feedback) in PROJECTS.md; built mimic-cursor on DUX (CC-BY-4.0) cursor strokes: 4 feedback conditions x 8 seeds x 30 rounds, cross-play, baselines, a data-copying check and a larger-budget ceiling search. Negative for the imitator (reference AUROC 0.99-1.00 in every condition; the ceiling stops at the replay baseline 0.88); two-way sharing gave the strongest detectors in cross-play, not significant at 8 seeds. DUX also carries webcam-derived emotion signals (~85 ms updates), the planned start for mimic-webcam.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: data sourcing and licence check, building and debugging a two-player search harness, 32-run experiment, analysis and write-up: about three working days for a research engineer

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
